title: Why the iPhone Duo is already cracking

lines.text: Apple's *two-thousand-dollar* foldable iPhone just came out, and screens are already *cracking*.
To see why, look *inside* the fold.
The screen is *ten* ultra-thin layers: a polymer cover, glass, the display, more glass, and a *titanium* plate.
When it closes, the outer layers travel *farther*, so an adhesive lets them *slide*.
Under it sits the *hinge*. iFixit rebuilt it from *CT scans*, and found three suspects.
One: the cracks sit where a cable *gap* meets the hinge, so stress hits the *same spot* every fold.
Two: curved rails may *lift* as it closes, right where the *damage* is.
Three: a speck of *dust*, pressed into the screen every close.
Apple hasn't said. Some cracks might just be a broken *connection*.
So close it *gently*, and send this to the friend who *pre-ordered*.
